node/10172955743.name: Rose Center for Earth and Space

node/10174524382.name: Union Square Drinking Fountain
node/10174524382.intro: Union Square Drinking Fountain, also known as James Fountain, is an outdoor bronze sculpture and ornamental fountain by Adolf von Donndorf and J. Leonard Corning. Cast in 1881 and dedicated on October 25, 1881, it was donated by Daniel Willis James and Theodore Roosevelt Sr.

node/10246738230.name: Benito Juárez
node/10246738230.intro: This is an outdoor bronze sculpture of Benito Juárez by Moises Cabrera Orozco in Bryant Park in Manhattan, New York. It was cast in Mexico in 2002 and installed on October 9, 2004.
node/10246738230.source_title: Statue of Benito Juárez (New York City)

node/10301699115.name: John Watts
node/10301699115.intro: An outdoor bronze sculpture depicting U.S. Congressman John Watts by George Edwin Bissell is installed in the Trinity Church Cemetery outside Manhattan's Trinity Church. It was erected by Watt's grandson, John Watts de Peyster, in 1893.

node/11186117026.name: Columbus
node/11186117026.intro: Columbus is a statue in Astoria, Queens created by Angelo Racioppi with funds from the New York City Works Progress Administration Art Project. Dedicated in 1941, it is in bronze on a cast stone base.

node/11435997070.name: Alexander Lyman Holley Monument
node/11435997070.intro: An outdoor bronze bust of Alexander Lyman Holley by artist John Quincy Adams Ward and architect Thomas Hastings is installed in Washington Square Park in Manhattan, New York. The monument was dedicated on October 2, 1890.

node/1242148250.name: New York Vietnam Veterans Memorial
node/1242148250.intro: Vietnam Veterans Plaza is an American memorial plaza in Manhattan, New York. It honors New York City citizens who served during the 20th-century Vietnam War.

node/1251496233.name: General Worth Monument
node/1251496233.intro: The General William Jenkins Worth Monument is a granite obelisk by James G. Batterson, installed in Manhattan's Worth Square, in the U.S. state of New York.

node/1251605864.name: Abraham Lincoln
node/1251605864.intro: This outdoor bronze statue of Abraham Lincoln by Henry Kirke Brown was installed in Union Square in Manhattan, New York on September 16th, 1870. It was sponsored by the Union League Club of New York.
node/1251605864.source_title: Statue of Abraham Lincoln (New York City)

node/1251605892.name: Marquis de Lafayette
node/1251605892.intro: Marquis de Lafayette is an outdoor bronze sculpture of Gilbert du Motier, Marquis de Lafayette by artist Frédéric Auguste Bartholdi. It is located at Union Square Park in Manhattan, New York.
node/1251605892.source_title: Statue of the Marquis de Lafayette (New York City)

node/12695294020.name: Needle Threading A Button
node/12695294020.intro: Needle Threading A Button is a public sculpture in the Garment District neighborhood of Manhattan, New York, located on 191 W 39th St. It is the district's first permanent art installation, being made out of stainless steel and aluminum.

node/12835627250.name: Triumph of Music
node/12835627250.intro: The Sources of Music and The Triumph of Music are two murals that Marc Chagall painted in 1966 for the Metropolitan Opera House at the Lincoln Center in New York City.

node/12835627251.source_title: The Sources of Music and The Triumph of Music

node/1289222423.name: José Bonifácio de Andrada e Silva
node/1289222423.intro: This is the Andrada Monument, an outdoor bronze sculpture of José Bonifácio de Andrada by José Otavio Correia Lima. It is 9 feet (2.7 m) tall and located at Bryant Park in Manhattan, New York.
node/1289222423.source_title: Statue of José Bonifácio de Andrada

node/1289222428.name: William Earl Dodge
node/1289222428.intro: William Earl Dodge is an outdoor bronze sculpture of William E. Dodge by John Quincy Adams Ward, located at Bryant Park in Manhattan, New York. It was cast in 1885 and dedicated on October 22 of that year.

node/1289222432.name: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
node/1289222432.intro: An outdoor bronze portrait bust of German writer Johann Wolfgang von Goethe by sculptor Karl Fischer is installed on the south side of Bryant Park in Manhattan, New York. It sits on a Swedish black granite pedestal.
node/1289222432.source_title: Bust of Johann Wolfgang von Goethe (New York City)

node/1289222452.name: Gertrude Stein
node/1289222452.intro: Gertrude Stein is an outdoor bronze sculpture of Gertrude Stein, located in Bryant Park in Manhattan in New York City. The casting was installed in 1992 and is based on a model created by Jo Davidson in Paris in 1923.

node/13016208878.name: SS Stevens Memorial Anchor
node/13016208878.intro: SS Stevens was a 473-foot (144 m), 14,893-ton ship that served as a floating dormitory from 1968 to 1975 for about 150 students of Stevens Institute of Technology. It was moored on the Hudson River across from New York City.

node/13025818444.name: Needle Threading A Button
node/13025818444.intro: Needle Threading A Button is a public sculpture in the Garment District neighborhood of Manhattan, New York, located on 191 W 39th St. It is the district's first permanent art installation, being made out of stainless steel and aluminum.

node/1329113669.name: Triumph of the Human Spirit
node/1329113669.intro: Triumph of the Human Spirit is a 2000 black granite sculpture by Lorenzo Pace, installed at Manhattan's Foley Square, in the U.S. state of New York. It was dedicated on Columbus Day, 2000.

node/1332501243.name: Prometheus
node/1332501243.intro: Prometheus is a 1934 gilded, cast bronze sculpture by Paul Manship, located above the lower plaza at Rockefeller Center in Manhattan, New York City.

node/13471557994.name: Triangle Fire Memorial
node/13471557994.intro: The Triangle Fire Memorial is a memorial at the Brown Building in the Greenwich Village neighborhood of Manhattan in New York City. It commemorates the 1911 Triangle Shirtwaist Factory fire, which killed 146 workers, primarily Italian and Jewish immigrant women and girls.

node/13732385972.name: New Museum
node/13732385972.intro: The New Museum of Contemporary Art is a museum at 235 Bowery, on the Lower East Side of Manhattan in New York City. It was founded in 1977 by Marcia Tucker.

node/14075405131.name: Frick Collection
node/14075405131.intro: The Frick Collection is an art museum on the Upper East Side of Manhattan in New York City. It was established in 1935 to preserve the collection of the industrialist Henry Clay Frick.

node/14181628740.name: Sunnyside Arch
node/14181628740.intro: The Sunnyside Arch is an illuminated steel arch spanning 46th Street just south of Queens Boulevard. Erected in 1983, the roughly two-story structure carries the neighborhood's name in lights.

node/1549441335.name: Dyckman Farmhouse Museum
node/1549441335.intro: The Dyckman House, now the Dyckman Farmhouse Museum, is a Dutch Colonial-style farmhouse at Broadway and 204th Street. It was the third built by William Dyckman, c. 1783–1785.

node/158809984.name: SoHo
node/158809984.intro: SoHo, short for "South of Houston Street", is a neighborhood in Lower Manhattan, New York City. Since the 1970s, it has been the location of many artists' lofts and art galleries.

node/1810241472.name: Rubin Museum of Art
node/1810241472.intro: The Rubin Museum of Himalayan Art is dedicated to the collection, display, and preservation of the art and cultures of the Himalayas, the Indian subcontinent, Central Asia and other regions within Eurasia. The museum closed on October 6, 2024.

node/1967476778.name: City Hall
node/1967476778.intro: The City Hall station, also known as City Hall Loop station, is a closed station on the IRT Lexington Avenue Line under City Hall Park. It opened on October 27, 1904, as one of the original 28 stations of the New York City Subway and closed on December 31, 1945.
node/1967476778.source_title: City Hall station (IRT Lexington Avenue Line)

node/2328643948.name: Harriet Tubman Memorial
node/2328643948.intro: The Harriet Tubman Memorial, also known as Swing Low, located in Manhattan in New York City, honors the life of abolitionist Harriet Tubman. It stands at 122nd Street, Frederick Douglass Boulevard, and St. Nicholas Avenue, now known as "Harriet Tubman Triangle".

node/2404084086.name: Weehawken 9/11 Memorial
node/2404084086.intro: The Hudson Riverfront 9/11 Memorial is in Weehawken, New Jersey. It commemorates the '9/11 boat lift', the emergency rescue response, and those who perished in the aftermath the September 11 attacks of the World Trade Center in 2001.

node/2435110791.name: George M. Cohan
node/2435110791.intro: A bronze sculpture of composer George M. Cohan by artist Georg John Lober and architect Otto Langman is installed at Duffy Square, part of Times Square, in the New York City borough of Manhattan.

node/2517056822.name: Flatiron District
node/2517056822.intro: The Flatiron District is a neighborhood in the borough of Manhattan of New York City, named for the Flatiron Building at 23rd Street, Broadway and Fifth Avenue.

node/2611640871.name: The Yankees Museum
node/2611640871.intro: The New York Yankees Museum is a sports museum located at Yankee Stadium on the main level at Gate 6. It is sponsored and presented by Bank of America and is dedicated to baseball memorabilia for the New York Yankees.

node/2639531695.name: Francis P. Duffy
node/2639531695.intro: An outdoor 1936–1937 statue of Francis P. Duffy by Charles Keck is installed at Duffy Square, part of Times Square. Titled Father Francis P. Duffy, it was dedicated on May 2, 1937.

node/2727025835.name: Alexander Hamilton
node/2727025835.intro: This is an outdoor granite sculpture of Alexander Hamilton by Carl Conrads in Central Park, Manhattan, New York. It was commissioned by Hamilton's son, John C. Hamilton, dedicated on November 22, 1880, and donated to the city.

node/2727025839.name: Balto
node/2727025839.intro: A bronze statue of Balto by Frederick Roth is installed in Central Park, Manhattan, New York. Balto led a team of sled dogs on the final leg of the 1925 serum run to Nome.

node/2727025884.name: 107th Infantry Memorial
node/2727025884.intro: The 107th Infantry Memorial is an outdoor bronze sculpture at the intersection of East 67th Street and Fifth Avenue in Central Park, Manhattan, New York. It honors members of the 107th Infantry who died during World War I.

node/2727025888.name: 7th Regiment Memorial
node/2727025888.intro: Seventh Regiment Memorial is an outdoor bronze sculpture atop a granite base honoring those members of the regiment who died during the Civil War. Although the statue is dated 1869 the monument was not unveiled until June 22, 1874.

node/2808008154.name: George Washington
node/2808008154.intro: George Washington is a large bronze sculpture of George Washington by John Quincy Adams Ward, installed on the front steps of Federal Hall National Memorial on Wall Street in New York City.

node/2808241058.name: Skyscraper Museum
node/2808241058.intro: The Skyscraper Museum is an architecture museum in the Battery Park City neighborhood of Manhattan in New York City, founded in 1996. It moved to its current and permanent location in Battery Park City in 2004.

node/3026462198.name: Court Street - Myrtle Avenue
node/3026462198.intro: Court Street and Myrtle Avenue was a station pair on the demolished BMT Fulton Street Line. It started service on April 24, 1888 and closed on June 1, 1940.
node/3026462198.source_title: Court Street and Myrtle Avenue stations

node/3026462201.name: Franklin Avenue
node/3026462201.intro: The Franklin Avenue station was a station on the demolished section of the BMT Myrtle Avenue Line. It was located at the intersection of Myrtle and Franklin Avenues in Bedford–Stuyvesant, Brooklyn, New York, United States, opened in 1889, and closed in 1969.
node/3026462201.source_title: Franklin Avenue station (BMT Myrtle Avenue Line)

node/3026462207.name: Grand Avenue
node/3026462207.intro: The Grand Avenue station was a station on the demolished section of the BMT Myrtle Avenue Line at the intersection of Myrtle Avenue and Grand Avenue in Brooklyn. It opened on April 27, 1889 and closed on January 21, 1953.
node/3026462207.source_title: Grand Avenue station (BMT Myrtle Avenue Line)

node/3026462210.name: Navy Street
node/3026462210.intro: The Navy Street station was a station on the demolished BMT Myrtle Avenue Line in Brooklyn, New York City. It opened on April 10, 1888 and closed on October 4, 1969, after a fire on the elevated structure.

node/3026462213.name: Nostrand Avenue
node/3026462213.intro: The Nostrand Avenue station was a station on the demolished section of the BMT Myrtle Avenue Line. The station was located at the intersection of Myrtle and Nostrand Avenues in Bedford–Stuyvesant, Brooklyn, opened in 1889, and closed in 1969.
node/3026462213.source_title: Nostrand Avenue station (BMT Myrtle Avenue Line)

node/3026462216.name: Sands Street
node/3026462216.intro: Sands Street was a station on the demolished BMT Myrtle Avenue Line. It was a large complex with two levels.

node/3026462225.name: Sumner Avenue
node/3026462225.intro: The Sumner Avenue station was a station on the demolished section of the BMT Myrtle Avenue Line. It was located at the intersection of Myrtle Avenue and Sumner Avenues in Bedford–Stuyvesant, Brooklyn, opened in 1889, and closed in 1969.
node/3026462225.source_title: Sumner Avenue station (BMT Myrtle Avenue Line)

node/3026462228.name: Tompkins Avenue
node/3026462228.intro: The Tompkins Avenue station was a station on the demolished section of the BMT Myrtle Avenue Line. The station opened in 1889, and closed in 1969.
node/3026462228.source_title: Tompkins Avenue station (BMT Myrtle Avenue Line)

node/3026462231.name: Vanderbilt Avenue
node/3026462231.intro: The Vanderbilt Avenue station was a station on the now-demolished BMT Myrtle Avenue Line in Brooklyn, New York City. It had two tracks and one island platform and closed on October 4, 1969, after a fire.
node/3026462231.source_title: Vanderbilt Avenue station (BMT Myrtle Avenue Line)

node/3026465034.name: Washington Avenue
node/3026465034.intro: The Washington Avenue station was a station on the demolished BMT Myrtle Avenue Line and BMT Lexington Avenue Line in Brooklyn, New York City. It was opened on December 4, 1888, and closed on October 4, 1969, after a fire on the structure.

node/3039734880.name: Fulton Street
node/3039734880.intro: The Fulton Street station was a station on the demolished section of the BMT Fifth Avenue Line in Brooklyn, New York City. It opened on July 27, 1889, and closed on May 31, 1940.
node/3039734880.source_title: Fulton Street station (BMT Fifth Avenue Line)

node/3039734896.name: Union Street
node/3039734896.intro: The Union Street station was a station on the demolished section of the BMT Fifth Avenue Line at the intersection of Fifth Avenue and Union Street. It opened on June 22, 1889 and closed on May 31, 1940.
node/3039734896.source_title: Union Street station (BMT Fifth Avenue Line)

node/3053660725.name: Albert Bertel Thorvaldsen
node/3053660725.intro: Bertel Thorvaldsen with the Statue of Hope is a self-portrait by Danish sculptor Bertel Thorvaldsen, created as a plaster model in his studio at Nysø Manor in 1839. It was executed in marble posthumously by Herman Wilhelm Bissen in 1859.
node/3053660725.source_title: Bertel Thorvaldsen with the Statue of Hope

node/3053660726.name: Daniel Webster
node/3053660726.intro: An outdoor bronze sculpture of Daniel Webster by Thomas Ball is installed in Central Park, Manhattan, New York. It was presented by Gordon W. Burnham in 1876.
node/3053660726.source_title: Statue of Daniel Webster (New York City)

node/3053660731.name: José Martí
node/3053660731.intro: A statue of José Martí by Anna Hyatt Huntington is installed in Manhattan's Central Park, in the U.S. state of New York.
node/3053660731.source_title: Equestrian statue of José Martí (Central Park)

node/3053660732.name: José de San Martín
node/3053660732.intro: An equestrian statue of José de San Martín by Louis-Joseph Daumas is installed in Manhattan's Central Park, in the U.S. state of New York. The sculpture was cast c. 1950 and dedicated on May 25, 1951.
node/3053660732.source_title: Equestrian statue of José de San Martín (Central Park)

node/3053662533.name: King Jagiello Monument
node/3053662533.intro: The King Jagiełło Monument is an equestrian monument of Władysław II Jagiełło, King of Poland and Grand Duke of Lithuania. It is located in Central Park, New York City.

node/3053662534.name: Ludwig van Beethoven
node/3053662534.intro: Ludwig van Beethoven is a series of sculptures of Ludwig van Beethoven by German-American sculptor Henry Baerer. The sculpture in Central Park was dedicated on July 22, 1884.

node/3053662565.name: Simón Bolívar
node/3053662565.intro: An equestrian statue of Simón Bolívar is installed in Manhattan's Central Park, in the U.S. state of New York. It was cast in 1919 and dedicated on April 19, 1921.
node/3053662565.source_title: Equestrian statue of Simón Bolívar (Central Park)

node/3070512789.name: America's Response Monument
node/3070512789.intro: America's Response Monument, subtitled De Oppresso Liber, is a life-and-a-half scale bronze statue in Liberty Park overlooking the National September 11 Memorial & Museum in New York City.

node/320948228.name: South Street Seaport
node/320948228.intro: The South Street Seaport is a historic area and neighborhood in the New York City borough of Manhattan, centered where Fulton Street meets the East River. It is within the Financial District of Lower Manhattan and is a designated historic district.

node/3224793125.name: American Folk Art Museum
node/3224793125.intro: The American Folk Art Museum is an art museum on the Upper West Side of Manhattan in New York City, at 2 Lincoln Square, Columbus Avenue at 66th Street. It is focused on the display and appreciation of folk art and works by contemporary self-taught artists.

node/3269867897.name: Eleanor Roosevelt Monument
node/3269867897.intro: The Eleanor Roosevelt Monument is located at the southeast corner of New York City's Riverside Park. Hillary Clinton gave the keynote address at the monument's dedication on October 5, 1996.

node/3271250895.name: Giuseppe Verdi Monument
node/3271250895.intro: The Giuseppe Verdi Monument is a sculpture honoring composer Giuseppe Verdi in Verdi Square Park in Manhattan, New York City. The statue was created by Italian sculptor Pasquale Civiletti.

node/3278932286.name: Delacorte Musical Clock
node/3278932286.intro: The Delacorte Clock, or George Delacorte Musical Clock, is a clock and art installation outside the Central Park Zoo in Central Park, Manhattan, New York. Dedicated in 1965, it is named for its benefactor George T. Delacorte Jr..

node/3341913861.name: Group of Bears
node/3341913861.intro: Group of Bears is a sculpture by Paul Manship.

node/3381640179.name: Joie de Vivre
node/3381640179.intro: Joie de Vivre is an outdoor sculpture by Mark di Suvero, located at Zuccotti Park. The 70-foot sculpture was installed by the intersection of Broadway and Cedar Street in June 2006.

node/3394722237.name: Non-Violence
node/3394722237.intro: Non-Violence, also known as The Knotted Gun, is a bronze sculpture by Swedish artist Carl Fredrik Reuterswärd of an oversized Colt Python .357 Magnum revolver with its barrel tied in a knot. It is located at the United Nations headquarters in New York City.

node/3421054404.name: Alamo
node/3421054404.intro: Alamo, also known as the Astor Place Cube or simply The Cube, is an outdoor sculpture by Tony Rosenthal. It is located on Astor Place, in the East Village neighborhood of Manhattan in New York City.

node/357607821.name: Stone Street Historic District
node/357607821.intro: Stone Street is a short street in the Financial District of Manhattan in New York City. The street, which runs in two sections, was originally a continuous roadway between Whitehall Street in the west and Hanover Square in the east.

node/357609892.name: Croton Reservoir
node/357609892.intro: The Croton Distributing Reservoir, also known as the Murray Hill Reservoir, was an above-ground reservoir at 42nd Street and Fifth Avenue in the New York City borough of Manhattan.

node/357618558.name: New York Studio School of Drawing, Painting and Sculpture
node/357618558.intro: The New York Studio School of Drawing, Painting and Sculpture is an art school at 8 West 8th Street in the Greenwich Village neighborhood of Manhattan. It was formed in 1963 by a group of students and their teacher, Mercedes Matter.
node/357618558.source_title: New York Studio School of Drawing, Painting and Sculpture

node/357620718.name: Richard Morris Hunt
node/357620718.intro: The Richard Morris Hunt Memorial is an exedra of granite and marble, dedicated to the memory of the architect Richard Morris Hunt. It was designed by Bruce Price with three sculptures by Daniel Chester French.

node/357642343.name: Audubon Terrace Historic District
node/357642343.intro: Audubon Terrace is a cultural complex comprising eight buildings in the Washington Heights neighborhood of Upper Manhattan, New York City, United States. Developed for several cultural institutions between 1904 and 1930, it was commissioned by Archer Milton Huntington.

node/357642349.name: Charlton-King-Vandam Historic District
node/357642349.intro: The Charlton–King–Vandam Historic District is a small historic district in Lower Manhattan, New York City. Designated by the New York City Landmarks Preservation Commission (NYCLPC) in 1966, it contains the city's largest concentration of row houses in the Federal style.

node/357642356.name: Hamilton Heights Historic District
node/357642356.intro: The Hamilton Heights Historic District is a national historic district in Hamilton Heights, New York, New York. It consists of 192 contributing residential rowhouses, apartment buildings, and churches built between about 1886 and 1931.

node/357642359.name: Henderson Place Historic District
node/357642359.intro: The Henderson Place Historic District is a historic district in the Yorkville neighborhood of Manhattan in New York City, New York, US. It includes 24 attached brick rowhouses, all designed by Lamb and Rich in the Queen Anne style.

node/357642362.name: Jumel Terrace Historic District
node/357642362.intro: The Jumel Terrace Historic District is in the Washington Heights neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City. It consists of 50 residential rowhouses built between 1890 and 1902, and one apartment building constructed in 1909.

node/357642364.name: Ladies Mile Historic District
node/357642364.intro: The Ladies' Mile Historic District was a prime shopping district in Manhattan, New York City, at the end of the 19th century, serving the well-to-do "carriage trade" of the city. It was designated in May 1989, by the New York City Landmark Preservation Commission.

node/357642372.name: Mount Morris Park Historic District
node/357642372.intro: Mount Morris Park Historic District is a 16-block historic district in west central Harlem, Manhattan, New York City. It was designated by the New York City Landmarks Preservation Commission in 1971.

node/357642380.name: Riverside-West 105th Street Historic District
node/357642380.intro: The Riverside–West 105th Street Historic District is on the Upper West Side of Manhattan in New York City, New York, US. It comprises rowhouses on Riverside Drive between 105th and 106th streets and on an adjacent block of 105th Street.

node/357642383.name: Riverside Drive-West 80th Street Historic District
node/357642383.intro: This is the Riverside Drive–West 80th–81st Streets Historic District on the Upper West Side of Manhattan in New York City, New York, US. It includes 32 attached rowhouses, built between 1892 and 1899.

node/357642387.name: Saint Mark's Historic District
node/357642387.intro: St. Mark's Historic District is a historic district located in the East Village neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City. It was designated a city landmark by the New York City Landmarks Preservation Commission in 1969.

node/357642394.name: Sniffen Court Historic District
node/357642394.intro: The Sniffen Court Historic District is a small close-ended mews in the Murray Hill neighborhood of Manhattan in New York City. It encompasses the entire alley, which consists of 10 two-story brick stables built in 1863–1864 in the early Romanesque Revival style.

node/357642403.name: Tudor City Historic District
node/357642403.intro: Tudor City is an apartment complex on the East Side of Manhattan in New York City, bordering the Turtle Bay and Murray Hill neighborhoods. Construction commenced in 1926, making it one of the first residential skyscraper complexes in the world.

node/357642406.name: Turtle Bay Gardens Historic District
node/357642406.intro: The Turtle Bay Gardens Historic District is a collection of twenty rowhouses in the Turtle Bay neighborhood of Manhattan in New York City. The rowhouses, dating from the 1860s, were renovated between 1918 and 1920 by Charlotte Hunnewell Sorchan to plans by Clarence Dean.

node/357642409.name: Upper East Side Historic District
node/357642409.intro: The Upper East Side Historic District is a historic district on the Upper East Side of Manhattan in New York City. First designated by the New York City Landmarks Preservation Commission in 1981, it was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1984.

node/357642449.name: Clinton Hill Historic District
node/357642449.intro: Clinton Hill Historic District is a national historic district in Clinton Hill, Brooklyn, in New York City. It consists of 1,063 largely residential contributing buildings built between the 1840s and 1930.

node/357650409.name: McCarthy Square
node/357650409.intro: McCarthy Square is a park in Manhattan, New York, named after Bernard Joseph McCarthy. The park and its memorial flagstaff, known as the Bernard McCarthy World War II Memorial, were dedicated in June 1943.

node/357742864.name: Flatrock Nature Center
node/357742864.intro: The Flat Rock Brook Nature Center is a 150-acre (0.61 km2) preserve and education center situated on the western slope of the Palisades in Englewood, New Jersey, United States of America. This nature center has 3.6 miles of trails.

node/367697388.name: Hoboken Historical Museum
node/367697388.intro: The Hoboken Historical Museum, founded in 1986, is located in Hoboken, New Jersey. In 2001, the museum moved to 1301 Hudson Street into the last standing building of the former Bethlehem Steel Hoboken Shipyard.

node/368043598.name: Stonewall Inn
node/368043598.intro: The Stonewall Inn is a gay bar and recreational tavern at 53 Christopher Street. It was the site of the 1969 Stonewall riots, which led to the gay liberation movement and the fight for LGBTQ+ rights in the United States.

node/368052754.name: Beacon Theater
node/368052754.intro: The Beacon Theatre at 2124 Broadway opened in 1929 as a movie palace developed by Samuel "Roxy" Rothafel. It was designed by Walter W. Ahlschlager and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

node/368061337.name: National Museum of the American Indian
node/368061337.intro: The National Museum of the American Indian–New York, the George Gustav Heye Center, is a branch of the National Museum of the American Indian at the Alexander Hamilton U.S. Custom House in Manhattan, New York City. The museum is part of the Smithsonian Institution.

node/368061518.name: Bronx Museum of the Arts
node/368061518.intro: The Bronx Museum of the Arts (BxMA), also called the Bronx Museum of Art or simply the Bronx Museum, is an American cultural institution located in Concourse, Bronx, New York. The museum is part of the Grand Concourse Historic District.

node/368061605.name: Yeshiva University Museum
node/368061605.intro: The Yeshiva University Museum is a teaching museum and the cultural arm of Yeshiva University. It is a member organization of the Center for Jewish History, a Smithsonian Institution affiliate located in the Chelsea neighborhood of Manhattan.

node/368061644.name: Museum of the Moving Image
node/368061644.intro: The Museum of the Moving Image (MoMI) is a time-based media museum located in a former building of the historic Astoria Studios, in the Astoria neighborhood of Queens in New York City. It originally opened in 1988 as the American Museum of the Moving Image.

node/368061648.name: New York Transit Museum
node/368061648.intro: The New York Transit Museum displays historical artifacts of the New York City Subway, bus, and commuter rail systems. The main museum is located in the decommissioned Court Street subway station in Downtown Brooklyn and Brooklyn Heights.

node/368061660.name: Lower East Side Tenement Museum
node/368061660.intro: The Lower East Side Tenement Museum is a museum and National Historic Site located at 97 and 103 Orchard Street. The two historical tenement buildings were home to an estimated 15,000 people, from over 20 nations, between 1863 and 1935 and 1888 and 2015.

node/373069793.name: Charging Bull
node/373069793.intro: Charging Bull is a bronze sculpture that stands on Broadway just north of Bowling Green in the Financial District of Manhattan in New York City.

node/3835410688.name: Alma Mater
node/3835410688.intro: Alma Mater is a bronze sculpture by Daniel Chester French on the steps of the Low Memorial Library on the campus of Columbia University. French designed the statue in 1901, and it was installed in September 1903.

node/3846182257.name: Alexander Hamilton
node/3846182257.intro: An outdoor 1908 sculpture of Alexander Hamilton by William Ordway Partridge is installed outside Hamilton Hall on the Columbia University campus in Manhattan, New York, United States.

node/3891884870.name: Victor Herbert
node/3891884870.intro: Victor Herbert is an outdoor bronze portrait bust of Victor Herbert by Edmond Thomas Quinn. It is located in Central Park in Manhattan, New York.

node/4224363289.name: Museum of Sex
node/4224363289.intro: The Museum of Sex, also known as MoSex, is a sex museum dedicated to preserving and presenting the history, evolution, and cultural significance of human sexuality. Visitors must be at least 18 years old due to explicit content in its educational exhibits.

node/422438959.name: Sir Walter Scott
node/422438959.intro: Sir Walter Scott is an outdoor bronze portrait statue of Walter Scott and the writer's favorite dog Maida by John Steell, located in Central Park in Manhattan, New York. It was cast in 1871 and dedicated on November 27, 1872.
node/422438959.source_title: Statue of Walter Scott (New York City)

node/422438963.name: Robert Burns
node/422438963.intro: Robert Burns is a bronze portrait statue of Robert Burns by John Steell. Four versions exist, in New York City, Dundee (Scotland), London (England), and Dunedin.

node/422438965.name: Christopher Columbus
node/422438965.intro: An outdoor bronze sculpture of Christopher Columbus by Jeronimo Suñol is installed in Central Park in Manhattan, New York.

node/424555887.name: George Washington
node/424555887.intro: George Washington is an outdoor sculpture by Henry Kirke Brown (1814–1886), located in Union Square, Manhattan. The bronze equestrian statue was dedicated in 1856 and is the oldest sculpture in the New York City Parks collection.
node/424555887.source_title: Equestrian statue of George Washington (New York City)

node/424555888.name: Mohandas Gandhi
node/424555888.intro: A statue of Mahatma Gandhi by Kantilal B. Patel stands in Union Square in Manhattan, New York, United States.
node/424555888.source_title: Statue of Mahatma Gandhi (New York City)

node/4252536496.name: National Museum of Mathematics
node/4252536496.intro: The National Museum of Mathematics or MoMath is a mathematics museum in Manhattan, New York City. The museum is known for a special tricycle with square wheels, which operates smoothly on a catenary surface.

node/4254512932.name: Samuel F. B. Morse
node/4254512932.intro: This is Samuel Finley Breese Morse, an outdoor bronze sculpture depicting American painter and inventor Samuel Morse by Byron M. Pickett, located in Central Park in Manhattan, New York. It was dedicated on June 10, 1871.

node/4290878204.name: Romeo and Juliet
node/4290878204.intro: Romeo and Juliet is an outdoor bronze sculpture by American artist Milton Hebald, located in front of Delacorte Theater in Manhattan's Central Park. Unveiled in 1977, it was donated by philanthropist George T. Delacorte, Jr.

node/4290878205.name: The Tempest
node/4290878205.intro: The Tempest is an outdoor bronze sculpture by Milton Hebald depicting Prospero and Miranda from William Shakespeare's The Tempest. Donated by George T. Delacorte, Jr. and unveiled in 1966, it is installed outside Delacorte Theater.

node/4314829890.name: Liz Christy Garden
node/4314829890.intro: The Liz Christy Bowery Houston Garden, officially started in 1974, is the first and oldest community garden in New York City. Located at the corner of the Bowery and Houston Street in Manhattan, it is now a part of New York City Parks Department.

node/4319650089.name: Colonnade row
node/4319650089.intro: Colonnade Row, also known as LaGrange Terrace, is a group of 1830s row houses on present-day Lafayette Street in the NoHo neighborhood of Manhattan in New York City. Four of the original nine row houses remain and are New York City designated landmarks.

node/432760466.name: Three Dancing Maidens – Untermyer Fountain
node/432760466.intro: Three Dancing Maidens is a nymph fountain (Nymphenbrunnen) sculpture by Walter Schott. One is known as the Untermyer Fountain in Central Park in New York City.

node/4408728261.name: Group of Four Trees
node/4408728261.intro: Group of Four Trees is an abstract outdoor sculpture completed in 1972 by the French artist Jean Dubuffet. It was Dubuffet's first outdoor sculpture installed in the United States.

node/4451144258.name: Temple of Dendur
node/4451144258.intro: The Temple of Dendur is a Roman Egyptian religious structure originally located in Tuzis, Nubia. Around 23 BCE, Emperor Augustus commissioned the temple dedicated to the Egyptian goddess Isis and deified brothers Pedesi and Pihor from Nubia.

node/4462440249.name: The Morgan Library & Museum
node/4462440249.intro: The Morgan Library & Museum is a museum and research library in New York City, New York, United States. Completed in 1906 as the private library of the banker J. P. Morgan, it is housed at 225 Madison Avenue in the Murray Hill neighborhood of Manhattan.

node/4470028591.name: Greenwich Village
node/4470028591.intro: Greenwich Village, or simply the Village, is a neighborhood on the west side of Lower Manhattan in New York City. It is bounded by 14th Street to the north, Broadway to the east, Houston Street to the south, and the Hudson River to the west.

node/4470030189.name: Gagosian
node/4470030189.intro: Gagosian Gallery is a modern and contemporary art gallery owned and directed by Larry Gagosian. As of 2024, Gagosian employs 300 people at 19 exhibition spaces.

node/4491242890.name: The Met Cloisters
node/4491242890.intro: The Cloisters is a museum in Fort Tryon Park, straddling the neighborhoods of Washington Heights and Inwood, in Upper Manhattan, New York City. It specializes in European medieval art and architecture, with a focus on the Romanesque and Gothic periods.

node/4672280505.name: Gay Liberation Monument
node/4672280505.intro: The Gay Liberation Monument is part of the Stonewall National Monument, which commemorates the Stonewall uprising of 1969. Created in 1980 by American artist George Segal, it was dedicated on June 23, 1992.

node/4726782722.name: Henry Ward Beecher Monument
node/4726782722.intro: The Henry Ward Beecher Monument is a statue of Henry Ward Beecher created by the sculptor John Quincy Adams Ward. It was unveiled on June 24, 1891, in Borough Hall Park, Brooklyn and later relocated to Cadman Plaza, Brooklyn in 1959.

node/4757184676.name: Fearless Girl
node/4757184676.intro: Fearless Girl is a bronze sculpture by Kristen Visbal of a 4-foot-high (1.2 m) girl standing in a self-confident pose. It is located in New York City on Broad Street across from the New York Stock Exchange Building in the Financial District of Manhattan.

node/4815674630.name: Strawberry Fields
node/4815674630.intro: Strawberry Fields is a two-and-a-half-acre (one-hectare) landscaped section in New York City's Central Park dedicated to the memory of former Beatles member John Lennon. It is named after the Beatles' song "Strawberry Fields Forever", written by Lennon.

node/5039268173.name: Brooklyn Heights Promenade
node/5039268173.intro: The Brooklyn Heights Promenade, also called the Esplanade, is a 1,826-foot-long (557 m) platform and pedestrian walkway in Brooklyn Heights, Brooklyn, New York City, United States. It is cantilevered over the Brooklyn-Queens Expressway.

node/5056373998.name: Double Check
node/5056373998.intro: Double Check is a 1982 sculpture by John Seward Johnson II. It is located across from Zuccotti Park at the corner of Liberty Street and Broadway in Manhattan, New York City.

node/5115375199.name: Japanese Peace Bell
node/5115375199.intro: The Japanese Peace Bell was donated to the United Nations Headquarters in New York City via the United Nations Association of Japan in June 1954. It was established by Chiyoji Nakagawa.

node/5265752909.name: The Albert Hotel
node/5265752909.intro: Hotel Albert, also known as The Albert and Albert Apartments, is a historic hotel and apartment complex located in the Greenwich Village neighborhood of Lower Manhattan, New York City. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2012.

node/5420936939.name: The Studio Museum In Harlem
node/5420936939.intro: The Studio Museum in Harlem is an African-American art museum at 144 West 125th Street. Founded in 1968, it collects, preserves and interprets art created by African Americans, members of the African diaspora, and artists from the African continent.

node/5509996164.name: The Renee and Chaim Gross Foundation
node/5509996164.intro: The Renee and Chaim Gross Foundation is a non-profit organization incorporated in 1989. It is located in the sculptor's four-story historic home on LaGuardia Place in Manhattan's Greenwich Village neighborhood.

node/561042174.name: The Sphere
node/561042174.intro: The Sphere is a monumental cast bronze sculpture by German artist Fritz Koenig.

node/561950053.name: William Shakespeare
node/561950053.intro: William Shakespeare is an outdoor bronze sculpture of William Shakespeare by John Quincy Adams Ward, located in Central Park in Manhattan, New York.
node/561950053.source_title: Statue of William Shakespeare (New York City)

node/561950133.name: Indian Hunter
node/561950133.intro: Indian Hunter is an outdoor bronze sculpture by John Quincy Adams Ward, located at Central Park in Manhattan, New York.

node/561950155.name: Fitz-Greene Halleck
node/561950155.intro: An outdoor bronze sculpture of Fitz-Greene Halleck by James Wilson Alexander MacDonald is installed in Central Park in Manhattan, New York. Cast in 1876 and installed in 1877, it was the first in Central Park depicting an American.

node/561950603.name: Alice in Wonderland
node/561950603.intro: The Alice in Wonderland is a sculpture located at Central Park in Manhattan, New York City, U.S. The bronze statue by Jose de Creeft stands eleven feet high.

node/5635158448.name: Arbitration Rock
node/5635158448.intro: The Arbitration Rock was set in 1769 as the boundary marker between the two Long Island townships of Newtown and Bushwick. Since Newtown was in Queens County and Bushwick in Kings County, it marked the dividing line between these two colonial New York counties.

node/5640186350.name: Mmuseumm
node/5640186350.intro: Mmuseumm is a modern natural history museum located in Tribeca, Lower Manhattan in New York City. The museum displays contemporary artifacts in a style reminiscent of the historical cabinet of curiosities model.

node/5654226941.name: Atlas
node/5654226941.intro: Atlas is a bronze statue in Rockefeller Center, within the International Building's courtyard, in Midtown Manhattan in New York City. The sculpture depicts the ancient Greek Titan Atlas holding the heavens on his shoulders.

node/5747425246.name: Center for Architecture
node/5747425246.intro: The Center for Architecture at 536 LaGuardia Place was designed by architect Andrew Berman and completed in 2003. It is operated by the New York Chapter of the American Institute of Architects.

node/5764181388.name: Frederick Douglass Memorial
node/5764181388.intro: This is the Frederick Douglass Memorial at the northwest corner of New York City's Central Park. It includes an 8-foot bronze sculpture by Gabriel Koren and was dedicated on September 20, 2011.

node/5849724991.name: Spyscape
node/5849724991.intro: Spyscape is a contemporary entertainment and education brand focused on secrets. Spyscape's physical HQ in New York City is a 60,000-square-foot interactive museum created by London-based private investment group Archimedia and designed by Sir David Adjaye.

node/5897336785.name: William Cullen Bryant
node/5897336785.intro: The William Cullen Bryant Memorial is an outdoor sculpture of William Cullen Bryant, located at Bryant Park in Manhattan, New York. The bronze statue was created by Herbert Adams and installed in 1911, the year the New York Public Library Main Branch building was completed.

node/5897336985.name: Golda Meir
node/5897336985.intro: Golda Meir is an outdoor bronze sculpture of former Israeli prime minister Golda Meir. It was unveiled in 1984 and is located at Golda Meir Square near Broadway and 39th Street in the Garment District of Manhattan, New York.

node/5927576885.name: Hangman's Elm
node/5927576885.intro: Hangman's Elm, or simply "The Hanging Tree", is an English elm located at the northwest corner in Washington Square Park in Greenwich Village, Manhattan, New York City. It stood at 135 feet (41 m) tall when measured c. 2000, and has a diameter of 67 inches (1.7 m).

node/5941231087.name: Metronome
node/5941231087.intro: Metronome is a large public art installation located along the south end of Union Square in New York City. The work was commissioned by the Related Companies, developers of One Union Square South, with the participation of the Public Art Fund and the Municipal Art Society.

node/5977004657.name: Myrtle Avenue Station
node/5977004657.intro: The Myrtle Avenue station was a station on the demolished BMT Lexington Avenue Line in Brooklyn, New York City. It was opened on May 13, 1885, and closed on October 13, 1950.
node/5977004657.source_title: Myrtle Avenue station (BMT Lexington Avenue Line)

node/5977004658.name: DeKalb Avenue Station
node/5977004658.intro: The DeKalb Avenue station was a station on the demolished BMT Lexington Avenue Line in Brooklyn, New York City. It was opened on May 13, 1885, and closed on October 13, 1950.
node/5977004658.source_title: DeKalb Avenue station (BMT Lexington Avenue Line)

node/5977004659.name: Greene Avenue Station
node/5977004659.intro: The Greene Avenue station was a station on the demolished BMT Lexington Avenue Line in Brooklyn, New York City. It was originally built on May 13, 1885, and closed on October 13, 1950.

node/5977004660.name: Franklin Avenue Station
node/5977004660.intro: The Franklin Avenue station was a station on the demolished BMT Lexington Avenue Line in Brooklyn, New York City. It was originally built on May 13, 1885 and closed on October 13, 1950.
node/5977004660.source_title: Franklin Avenue station (BMT Lexington Avenue Line)

node/5977004662.name: Tompkins Avenue Station
node/5977004662.intro: The Tompkins Avenue station was a station on the demolished BMT Lexington Avenue Line in Brooklyn, New York City. It opened on May 13, 1885, and closed on October 13, 1950.
node/5977004662.source_title: Tompkins Avenue station (BMT Lexington Avenue Line)

node/5977004663.name: Sumner Avenue Station
node/5977004663.intro: The Sumner Avenue station was a station on the demolished BMT Lexington Avenue Line in Brooklyn, New York City. It was opened on May 13, 1885, and closed on October 13, 1950.
node/5977004663.source_title: Sumner Avenue station (BMT Lexington Avenue Line)

node/5977004664.name: Reid Avenue Station
node/5977004664.intro: The Reid Avenue station was a station on the demolished BMT Lexington Avenue Line in Brooklyn, New York City. It was opened on May 13, 1885, and closed on October 13, 1950.
node/5977004664.source_title: Reid Avenue station (BMT Lexington Avenue Line)

node/5995383978.name: Roseland Ballroom
node/5995383978.intro: The Roseland Ballroom was a multipurpose hall, in a converted ice skating rink. It was in New York City's theater district, on West 52nd Street in Manhattan.

node/600524075.name: Burnett Memorial Fountain
node/600524075.intro: Frances Hodgson Burnett Memorial Fountain, near Fifth Avenue and the Museum of the City of New York in Manhattan's Central Park, is an outdoor bronze sculpture and fountain. It serves as a memorial to Burnett, the author of The Secret Garden and Little Lord Fauntleroy.

node/6259917258.name: Thomas Jefferson
node/6259917258.intro: An outdoor sculpture of Thomas Jefferson by William Ordway Partridge is installed outside the School of Journalism on the Columbia University campus. It was modeled in plaster in 1901 and cast in bronze in 1914 by Roman Bronze Works.

node/6271960188.name: The Garment Worker
node/6271960188.intro: The Garment Worker, created by Judith Weller, is a realistic rendering of a garment worker, wearing a yarmulke and bent over a hand-operated sewing machine. The sculpture is based on Weller's father, who was a machine operator in the garment industry in New York.

node/6456605729.name: Dante Alighieri
node/6456605729.intro: This is a statue of the Italian poet Dante Alighieri dedicated in 1921. It is in Dante Park in Manhattan, New York City.

node/6572519247.name: Life Underground
node/6572519247.intro: Life Underground (2001) is a permanent public artwork created by American sculptor Tom Otterness for the New York City Subway's 14th Street/Eighth Avenue station. The station serves the A, C, E, and L trains.

node/6925436185.name: Joker Stairs
node/6925436185.intro: The West 167th Street Stairs, colloquially known as the Joker Stairs, are a step street connecting Shakespeare and Anderson avenues at West 167th Street. The stairs served as one of the filming locations for the 2019 film Joker.

node/7096788484.name: Sphere Within Sphere
node/7096788484.intro: Sphere Within Sphere describes a series of spherical bronze sculptures by Italian sculptor Arnaldo Pomodoro. In 1966, Pomodoro was commissioned to create a 3.5-meter sphere for Expo 67 in Montreal.

node/726445300.name: Amiable Child Memorial
node/726445300.intro: The Amiable Child Monument is a monument located in New York City's Riverside Park.

node/7298030172.name: Reclining Figure
node/7298030172.intro: Reclining Figure (Lincoln Center) (LH 519) is a statue by Henry Moore. The original two-part bronze statue was commissioned for the Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts in New York City and has been displayed outdoors since 1965.

node/7393740455.name: New York Central Railroad 69th Street Transfer Bridge
node/7393740455.intro: The 69th Street Transfer Bridge was a dock for car floats on the Upper West Side of Manhattan in New York City, United States. It allowed the transfer of railroad cars to car floats which crossed the Hudson River to the Weehawken Yards in New Jersey.
node/7393740455.source_title: New York Central Railroad 69th Street Transfer Bridge

node/8270992264.name: National Jazz Museum in Harlem
node/8270992264.intro: The National Jazz Museum in Harlem is dedicated to preservation and celebration of the jazz history, culture and music of Harlem, Manhattan, New York City. For more than 15 years, the museum was in East Harlem at 104 East 126th Street.

node/8307408828.name: Malcolm X & Dr. Betty Shabazz Memorial and Educational Center
node/8307408828.intro: The Malcolm X and Dr. Betty Shabazz Memorial and Educational Center is a memorial to Malcolm X and Betty Shabazz located at 3940 Broadway and West 165th Street. It opened on May 19, 2005, the 80th anniversary of Malcolm X's birth.
node/8307408828.source_title: Malcolm X and Dr. Betty Shabazz Memorial and Educational Center

node/8379857649.name: Bellerophon Taming Pegasus
node/8379857649.intro: Bellerophon Taming Pegasus is an outdoor sculpture by Jacques Lipchitz, depicting Bellerophon and Pegasus. It was the final sculpture worked on by Lipchitz, and was completed after his death in 1973.

node/8529577188.name: Women's Rights Pioneers Monument
node/8529577188.intro: The Women's Rights Pioneers Monument is a sculpture by Meredith Bergmann, installed in Central Park, Manhattan, New York City, on August 26, 2020. It depicts Sojourner Truth, Susan B. Anthony (1820–1906), and Elizabeth Cady Stanton (1815–1902).

node/8873729191.name: Eagles and Prey
node/8873729191.intro: Eagles and Prey is an outdoor bronze sculpture by Christophe Fratin, located in Central Park in Manhattan, New York. Created in 1850 and installed in Central Park in 1863, it is the earliest known sculpture to be installed in any New York City park.

node/8873736445.name: The Falconer
node/8873736445.intro: The Falconer is a bronze sculpture in Central Park, New York City by English sculptor George Blackall Simonds. It depicts a man in a theatrical version of Elizabethan dress standing on a high granite pedestal, releasing a hunting falcon.

node/8881531828.name: Giuseppe Garibaldi
node/8881531828.intro: An outdoor bronze sculpture of Giuseppe Garibaldi, one of the leaders of Italian unification, is installed in Washington Square Park in Manhattan, New York.
node/8881531828.source_title: Statue of Giuseppe Garibaldi (New York City)

node/8881619455.name: Giuseppe Mazzini
node/8881619455.intro: An outdoor bronze bust of Giuseppe Mazzini by Giovanni Turini is installed in Central Park's Sheep Meadow, in Manhattan, New York. It was dedicated in 1878 with a speech by American poet William Cullen Bryant.

node/8942135848.name: The Africa Center
node/8942135848.intro: The Africa Center is a museum located at Fifth Avenue and 110th Street in East Harlem, Manhattan, New York City. Founded in 1984, it is dedicated to increasing public understanding and appreciation of African art and culture.

node/8942168458.name: Museum of Contemporary African Diasporan Arts
node/8942168458.intro: The Museum of Contemporary African Diasporan Arts (MoCADA), is Brooklyn's first and only contemporary art museum dedicated to the art and culture of Africa and its diaspora. Since 2023, the museum has operated within an expanded campus which includes three venues:
node/8942168458.source_title: Museum of Contemporary African Diasporan Arts

node/9035436348.name: Unity
node/9035436348.intro: Unity is a 22-foot (6.7 m) tall bronze sculpture of an arm, hand, and pointing index finger by Hank Willis Thomas, installed in Brooklyn, New York City. The artwork was unveiled in 2019.

node/9136326361.name: Leslie-Lohman Museum of Art
node/9136326361.intro: The Leslie-Lohman Museum of Art (LLMA) is a visual art museum in SoHo, Lower Manhattan, New York City. It owns more than 22,000 objects, including, paintings, drawings, photography, prints and sculpture.

node/9470799318.name: New York Earth Room
node/9470799318.intro: The New York Earth Room is an interior sculpture by the artist Walter De Maria. It has been installed in a loft at 141 Wooster Street in the Tribeca neighborhood of New York City since 1977.

node/9484120671.name: Tightrope Walker
node/9484120671.intro: Tightrope Walker is an outdoor bronze sculpture by Dutch artist Kees Verkade, installed on Columbia University's Revson Plaza in 1979. The work commemorates General William J. Donovan.

relation/10571875.name: Duke Ellington Circle
relation/10571875.intro: Duke Ellington Circle is a traffic circle at the northeast corner of Central Park at the intersection of Fifth Avenue and 110th Street in Harlem, Manhattan, New York City. It is named for the jazz musician Duke Ellington.

relation/11077079.name: African Burial Ground National Monument
relation/11077079.intro: African Burial Ground National Monument is a monument at Duane Street and African Burial Ground Way in the Civic Center section of Lower Manhattan, New York City. Its main building is the Ted Weiss Federal Building at 290 Broadway.

relation/1341944.name: The Dakota
relation/1341944.intro: The Dakota, also known as the Dakota Apartments, is a cooperative apartment building at 1 West 72nd Street. It was constructed between 1880 and 1884 in the German Renaissance style and was designed by Henry Janeway Hardenbergh.

relation/13902286.name: McCarren Park
relation/13902286.intro: McCarren Park is a public park in Brooklyn, New York City. It is located on the border of Williamsburg and Greenpoint and is bordered by Nassau Avenue, Bayard Street, Lorimer Street and North 12th Street.

relation/14425097.name: Saint Vartan Park
relation/14425097.intro: St. Vartan Park is a 2.76-acre (1.12 ha) public park in the Murray Hill neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City. Originally called St. Gabriel's Park, it was renamed in 1978 after St. Vartan Armenian Cathedral.

relation/14735368.name: Henry Hudson Park
relation/14735368.intro: Henry Hudson Memorial Park is a small public park in the Spuyten Duyvil neighborhood of The Bronx in New York City, located at the intersection of Kappock Street and Independence Avenue. It is the site of the Henry Hudson Monument or Henry Hudson Memorial, dedicated in 1938.

relation/14982184.name: Macombs Dam Park
relation/14982184.intro: Macombs Dam Park is a park in the Concourse section of the Bronx, New York City. It is between Jerome Avenue and the Major Deegan Expressway, near the Harlem River and the Macombs Dam Bridge.

relation/15902634.name: Brooklyn Banks
relation/15902634.intro: Brooklyn Banks is an area under the Manhattan side of the Brooklyn Bridge in New York City. It is a skate spot popular among skateboarders and BMXers for brick banked surfaces, benches, pillars, ledges, stairs, and handrails.

relation/16231018.name: Vessel
relation/16231018.intro: Vessel is a 16-story, 150-foot-tall (46 m) structure of connected staircases in the 5-acre (2.0 ha) Hudson Yards Public Square of Hudson Yards in Manhattan, New York City.

relation/16711715.name: Grand Army Plaza
relation/16711715.intro: Grand Army Plaza is a public square at the southeast corner of Central Park in Manhattan, New York City, near the intersection of Fifth Avenue and Central Park South. The current design dates to a 1916 reconstruction by the architectural firm of Carrère and Hastings.

relation/17229873.name: Riverside Park
relation/17229873.intro: Riverside Park is a scenic waterfront public park along the Hudson River on the West Side of the borough of Manhattan in New York City. It measures 4 miles (6.4 km) long and 100 to 500 feet wide, running from 72nd to 158th Street.

relation/17233746.name: Manhattan Bridge
relation/17233746.intro: The Manhattan Bridge is a suspension bridge that crosses the East River in New York City, connecting Lower Manhattan at Canal Street with Downtown Brooklyn at the Flatbush Avenue Extension. Designed by Leon Moisseiff, it has a total length of 6,855 ft (2,089 m).

relation/17290189.name: Cadman Plaza Park
relation/17290189.intro: Cadman Plaza is a park on the border of the Brooklyn Heights and Downtown Brooklyn neighborhoods in Brooklyn, New York City. Named for Reverend Doctor Samuel Parkes Cadman (1864–1936), it was named as a park in 1939.

relation/1751075.name: John Jay Park
relation/1751075.intro: John Jay Park is a 3.3-acre (13,000 m2) park in the New York City borough of Manhattan. It is located between East 76th and 78th Streets, and between the FDR Drive and a short street called Cherokee Place, on Manhattan's Upper East Side.

relation/18351439.name: Rockefeller Center
relation/18351439.intro: Rockefeller Center is a complex of 19 commercial buildings covering 22 acres (8.9 ha) between 48th Street and 51st Street. The 14 original Art Deco buildings, commissioned by the Rockefeller family, span the area between Fifth Avenue and Sixth Avenue.

relation/20781110.name: Inwood Hill Park
relation/20781110.intro: Inwood Hill Park is a 196 acres (79 ha) public park in the Inwood neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City, operated by the New York City Department of Parks and Recreation. It contains the largest remaining old-growth forest on the island of Manhattan.

relation/20812866.name: Hudson River Park
relation/20812866.intro: Hudson River Park is a waterfront park and marine reserve along the Hudson River on the west side of Manhattan in New York City. The 4.5-mile (7.2 km) linear park extends from 59th Street south to Battery Park.

relation/2389631.name: Governors Island
relation/2389631.intro: Governors Island is a 172-acre (70 ha) island in New York Harbor, within the New York City borough of Manhattan. The Trust for Governors Island operates the remaining 150 acres (61 ha), including 52 historic buildings, as a public park.

relation/3314082.name: Eagle Warehouse & Storage Company
relation/3314082.intro: The Eagle Warehouse & Storage Company is a building in the Dumbo and Brooklyn Heights neighborhoods of Brooklyn in New York City. Designed by Brooklyn architect Frank Freeman and completed in 1894, it was converted into apartments in 1980.

relation/3582905.name: Building at 45 East 66th Street
relation/3582905.intro: 45 East 66th Street is a cooperative apartment building on the Upper East Side of Manhattan in New York City, United States. It was built between 1906 and 1908 and was designed by the firm of Harde & Short.

relation/3606825.name: New-York Historical Society
relation/3606825.intro: The New York Historical is an American history museum and library on the Upper West Side of Manhattan in New York City. The society was founded in 1804 as New York's first museum.

relation/3606980.name: Apthorp Apartments
relation/3606980.intro: The Apthorp is a condominium building at 2211 Broadway on the Upper West Side of Manhattan in New York City. It was built between 1905 and 1908 as a residential hotel by William Waldorf Astor and is a New York City designated landmark.

relation/3624833.name: Cathedral of Saint John the Divine
relation/3624833.intro: The Cathedral of St. John the Divine is the cathedral of the Episcopal Diocese of New York. It is at 1047 Amsterdam Avenue in the Morningside Heights neighborhood of Manhattan in New York City, between West 110th Street and West 113th Street.
relation/3624833.source_title: Cathedral of St. John the Divine

relation/3690816.name: Highbridge Park
relation/3690816.intro: Highbridge Park is a public park on the western bank of the Harlem River in Washington Heights, Manhattan, New York City. It stretches between 155th Street and Dyckman Street in Upper Manhattan.

relation/3695753.name: Alexander Hamilton U.S. Custom House
relation/3695753.intro: The Alexander Hamilton U.S. Custom House is at 1 Bowling Green, near the southern end of Manhattan. Designed by Cass Gilbert in the Beaux-Arts style, it was erected from 1902 to 1907 as a headquarters for the Port of New York's duty collection operations.

relation/3695755.name: Castle Clinton
relation/3695755.intro: Castle Clinton is a restored circular sandstone fort within Battery Park at the southern end of Manhattan in New York City, United States. Built from 1808 to 1811, it was the first American immigration station, predating Ellis Island.

relation/3698894.name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
relation/3698894.intro: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, colloquially referred to as the Met, is an encyclopedic art museum in New York City. By floor area, it is the fourth-largest museum in the world and the largest art museum in the Americas.

relation/3700068.name: Castle Williams
relation/3700068.intro: Castle Williams is a circular fortification of red sandstone on the northwest point of Governors Island. Together with Fort Jay, it is managed by the National Park Service as part of Governors Island National Monument.

relation/3910502.name: Aqueduct Walk
relation/3910502.intro: Aqueduct Walk is a linear public park in the West Bronx in New York City, New York. It stretches about 1.7 miles (2.7 km) between Kingsbridge Road to the north and Tremont Avenue to the south.

relation/4099553.name: Sara D. Roosevelt Park
