way/230757260.intro: The Brooklyn Heights Promenade, also called the Esplanade, is a 1,826-foot-long (557 m) platform and pedestrian walkway cantilevered over the Brooklyn-Queens Expressway. It is in Brooklyn Heights, Brooklyn, New York City, United States.

way/231847469.name: Socrates Sculpture Park
way/231847469.intro: Socrates Sculpture Park is an outdoor museum and public park where artists can create and exhibit sculptures and multi-media installations. It offers an arts education program, artist residency program, and job training.

way/238974585.name: Pepsi-Cola Sign
way/238974585.intro: The Pepsi-Cola sign is a neon sign at Gantry Plaza State Park in the Long Island City neighborhood of Queens in New York City. It was built in 1940 and originally installed atop PepsiCo's bottling factory nearby.

way/239795718.name: Bushwick Inlet Park
way/239795718.intro: Bushwick Inlet Park is a public park in the Williamsburg and Greenpoint neighborhoods of Brooklyn, New York City. It is located along the East River and named for the nearby Bushwick Inlet.

way/239977366.name: Vesuvio Playground
way/239977366.intro: Vesuvio Playground is an 0.64-acre (2,600 m2) neighborhood park located on the corner of Thompson Street and Spring Street, off Prince Street, in SoHo, Manhattan, New York City.

way/239988106.name: Spring Street Park
way/239988106.intro: Spring Street Park is a small triangular park in the lower Manhattan neighborhood of Hudson Square in New York City. As a pedestrian plaza, the triangle was previously known as SoHo Square.

way/241833034.name: Center for Brooklyn History
way/241833034.intro: The Center for Brooklyn History is a museum, library branch, and educational center in Brooklyn, New York, United States. Part of the Brooklyn Public Library (BPL) system, it is located at 128 Pierrepont Street in Brooklyn Heights.

way/241833272.name: The Ukrainian Museum
way/241833272.intro: The Ukrainian Museum, founded in 1976 by the Ukrainian National Women's League of America in New York City, is the largest museum of its kind outside of Ukraine.

way/241850633.name: Coignet Building
way/241850633.intro: The Coignet Stone Company Building is a historical structure in the Gowanus neighborhood of Brooklyn in New York City, United States. Designed by architects William Field and Son and constructed between 1872 and 1873, it is the city's oldest remaining concrete building.

way/244978444.name: Winston Churchill Square
way/244978444.intro: Sir Winston Churchill Square is a .05-acre (0.020 ha) garden and sitting area in the Greenwich Village neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City. It is at the southwest corner of Bleecker Street, Downing Street, and Sixth Avenue.

way/247838607.name: Merchant's House Museum
way/247838607.intro: The Merchant's House Museum, also known as the Old Merchant's House and the Seabury Tredwell House, is at 29 East Fourth Street. Built by the hatter Joseph Brewster in 1831 and 1832, it was the Tredwell family's residence for almost a century before becoming a museum in 1936.

way/247867323.name: 240 Centre Street
way/247867323.intro: 240 Centre Street, formerly the New York City Police Headquarters, was the headquarters of the New York City Police Department (NYPD) from 1909 to 1973. Designed by the firm Hoppin & Koen, it is a New York City designated landmark and on the National Register of Historic Places.

way/248166269.name: Washington Square Arch
way/248166269.intro: The Washington Square Arch, officially the Washington Arch, is a marble memorial arch at the Washington Square Park. Designed by architect Stanford White in 1891, it commemorates the centennial of George Washington's 1789 inauguration as President of the United States.

way/249664005.name: Stonewall Inn State Historic Site
way/249664005.intro: The Stonewall Inn is a gay bar and recreational tavern at 53 Christopher Street. It was the site of the 1969 Stonewall riots.

way/249664327.name: The Drawing Center
way/249664327.intro: The Drawing Center is a museum and a nonprofit exhibition space in Manhattan, New York City, that focuses on the exhibition of drawings, both historical and contemporary.

way/249664614.name: New York City Fire Museum
way/249664614.intro: The New York City Fire Museum is a museum dedicated to the New York City Fire Department (FDNY) in the Hudson Square neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City. It is housed in the former quarters of the FDNY's Engine Company No. 30, a renovated 1904 fire house.

way/250052723.name: FDNY Ladder 8
way/250052723.intro: Firehouse, Hook & Ladder Company 8 is a New York City Fire Department (FDNY) fire station at 14 North Moore Street in the Tribeca neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City. Its exterior appeared in the supernatural comedy franchise Ghostbusters.

way/25026338.name: Zuccotti Park
way/25026338.intro: Zuccotti Park is a 33,000-square-foot (3,100 m2) publicly accessible park in the Financial District of Lower Manhattan in New York City. It is bounded by Broadway to the east, Liberty Street to the north, Trinity Place to the west, and Cedar Street to the south.

way/250267911.name: Museum at Eldridge Street
way/250267911.intro: The Museum at Eldridge Street, founded in 1986 as the Eldridge Street Project, occupies the synagogue under a long-term lease. The synagogue was built in 1887 for Congregation Kahal Adath Jeshurun.

way/250386859.name: Quarters A
way/250386859.intro: Quarters A, also known as the Commandant's House, is a historic house on Evans Street in the Vinegar Hill neighborhood of Brooklyn, New York City. Built beginning in 1805, it was designated a National Historic Landmark in 1974.

way/25162896.name: Tompkins Square Park
way/25162896.intro: Tompkins Square Park is a 10.5-acre (4.2 ha) public park in the Alphabet City portion of East Village, Manhattan, New York City. The park opened in 1834 and is named for Daniel D. Tompkins, Vice President of the United States.

way/253824514.name: The Ansonia
way/253824514.intro: The Ansonia is a condominium building at 2109 Broadway, between 73rd and 74th Streets, on the Upper West Side of Manhattan in New York City, New York, United States. It was built between 1899 and 1903 as a residential hotel by William Earle Dodge Stokes.

way/25420828.name: Joe Sabba Park
way/25420828.intro: Joe Sabba Park is a 0.47-acre (1,900 m2) New York City public park in the Sunnyside neighborhood of Queens in New York City. It is named after Joe Sabba, a veteran of World War II and local activist from Sunnyside.

way/25428484.name: Gantry Plaza State Park
way/25428484.intro: Gantry Plaza State Park is a 12-acre (4.9 ha) state park on the East River in the Hunters Point section of Long Island City. It includes a collection of gantries with car float transfer bridges.

way/263202827.name: Fireboat John J. Harvey
way/263202827.intro: John J. Harvey is a fireboat formerly of the New York City Fire Department (FDNY). She is capable of pumping up to 18,000 gallons of water a minute and returned to service following the September 11, 2001 attacks.

way/263202828.name: Lightship Frying Pan
way/263202828.intro: Frying Pan (LV-115) is a lightvessel moored at Pier 66a in the Chelsea neighborhood of Manhattan in New York City. It served at Frying Pan Shoals, off Cape Fear in North Carolina, for over 30 years.

way/264003876.name: Paley Park
way/264003876.intro: Paley Park is a pocket park located at 3 East 53rd Street between Madison and Fifth Avenues in Midtown Manhattan, New York City. It opened May 23, 1967.

way/264647249.name: Women’s Liberation Center
way/264647249.intro: The Women's Liberation Center (WLC) is a historic building and former organization in the Chelsea neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City, New York. It operated from 1972 to 1987 and was also known as the Women's Firehouse.

way/264768896.name: Flatiron Building
way/264768896.intro: The Flatiron Building is a 22-story, 307-foot-tall (93.6 m) building at 175 Fifth Avenue in Manhattan in New York City, New York, US. Designed by Daniel Burnham and Frederick P. Dinkelberg, it opened in 1902.

way/265302076.name: Stephen A. Schwarzman Building
way/265302076.intro: The Stephen A. Schwarzman Building is the flagship building in the New York Public Library system in the Midtown neighborhood of Manhattan in New York City. The branch, one of four research libraries in the library system, has nine divisions.
way/265302076.source_title: New York Public Library Main Branch

way/265355138.name: Church of Saint Paul the Apostle
way/265355138.intro: The Church of St. Paul the Apostle is a Catholic church on the Upper West Side of Manhattan in New York City. It is the mother church of the Paulist Fathers, the first religious community of Catholic priests founded in the United States.

way/265357846.name: Intrepid Museum
way/265357846.intro: The Intrepid Museum is a military, aerospace, and history museum in New York City, United States. It is located at Pier 86 at 46th Street, along the Hudson River, in the Hell's Kitchen neighborhood on the West Side of Manhattan.

way/265875544.name: Joseph Raphael De Lamar House
way/265875544.intro: The Joseph Raphael De Lamar House at 233 Madison Avenue was built from 1902 to 1905. The five-story house was designed by C. P. H. Gilbert in the Beaux-Arts style for Joseph Raphael De Lamar.

way/265947358.name: Grand Central Terminal
way/265947358.intro: Grand Central Terminal is a commuter rail terminal at 42nd Street and Park Avenue in Midtown Manhattan, New York City. Grand Central is the southern terminus of the Metro-North Railroad's Harlem, Hudson and New Haven Lines.

way/266010379.name: Saint Patrick’s Cathedral
way/266010379.intro: St. Patrick's Cathedral is a Catholic cathedral in the Midtown Manhattan neighborhood of New York City, United States. It is the seat of the Archbishop of New York as well as a parish church.

way/266077859.name: Hells Kitchen Park
way/266077859.intro: Hell's Kitchen Park is a 0.58-acre (0.23 ha) park in Hell's Kitchen in Manhattan, New York City.

way/266170658.name: The Penn Club
way/266170658.intro: 30 West 44th Street is the clubhouse of the Penn Club of New York in the Midtown Manhattan neighborhood of New York City. Designed by architecture firm Tracy and Swartwout in the Beaux-Arts style, it opened in 1901 as the Yale Club of New York City's clubhouse.

way/266199252.name: Mount Vernon Hotel Museum
way/266199252.intro: The Mount Vernon Hotel Museum & Garden, formerly the Abigail Adams Smith Museum, is an antebellum building. Since 1924, it has been operated by the Colonial Dames of America.

way/266886536.name: Park Avenue Armory
way/266886536.intro: The Park Avenue Armory, also known as the 7th Regiment Armory, is a historic armory at 643 Park Avenue. It was designed in the Gothic Revival style by Charles Clinton and completed in 1880.

way/266887857.name: Asia Society
way/266887857.intro: The Asia Society is a 501(c)(3) organization that focuses on educating the world about Asia. Its headquarters are in New York City, and includes a museum that exhibits pre-modern, modern, and contemporary art from Asia, Oceania and the Asian diaspora.

way/266894185.name: Henry Clay Frick House
way/266894185.intro: The Henry Clay Frick House is a mansion and museum building on Fifth Avenue, between 70th and 71st streets. Designed by Thomas Hastings as the residence of the industrialist Henry Clay Frick, it contains the Frick Collection museum and the Frick Art Reference Library.

way/266899031.name: Payne Whitney House
way/266899031.intro: The Payne Whitney House at 972 Fifth Avenue was completed in 1909 as a private residence for businessman William Payne Whitney and his family. It was designed in the High Italian Renaissance style by architect Stanford White of the firm McKim, Mead & White.

way/266926165.name: Apartment at 1261 Madison Avenue
way/266926165.intro: 1261 Madison Avenue is an apartment building on the Upper East Side of Manhattan in New York City, New York, US. It was built between 1900 and 1901 and was designed by the firm of Buchman & Fox.

way/266926168.name: Cooper–Hewitt, Smithsonian Design Museum
way/266926168.intro: The Andrew Carnegie Mansion at 2 East 91st Street was completed in 1902 for the industrialist Andrew Carnegie, his wife Louise, and their only child Margaret. Since 1976, the house has been occupied by the Cooper-Hewitt Museum, part of the Smithsonian Institution.

way/266926271.name: Otto H. Kahn House
way/266926271.intro: The Otto H. Kahn House is a mansion at 1 East 91st Street, at Fifth Avenue. It was completed in 1918 as the town residence of the financier and philanthropist Otto H. Kahn and his family.

way/266930863.name: Building at 133 East 80th Street
way/266930863.intro: 133 East 80th Street is a cooperative apartment building on the Upper East Side of Manhattan, New York City, United States. Designed by Rosario Candela, the 15-story building opened in October 1930 and was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 2010.

way/266934250.name: Institute for the Study of the Ancient World
way/266934250.intro: The Institute for the Study of the Ancient World (ISAW) is a center for advanced scholarly research and graduate education at New York University. Its mission is to cultivate comparative, connective investigations of the ancient world from the western Mediterranean to China.
way/266934250.source_title: Institute for the Study of the Ancient World

way/266934254.name: Neue Galerie New York
way/266934254.intro: The Neue Galerie New York is a museum of early twentieth-century German and Austrian art and design on the Upper East Side of Manhattan in New York City. It is located in the William Starr Miller House at 86th Street and Fifth Avenue.

way/266940034.name: George F. Baker Jr. and Sr. Houses
way/266940034.intro: The George F. Baker Jr. Houses are a complex of three residential buildings at 67, 69, and 75 East 93rd Street on the Upper East Side of Manhattan in New York City. They were completed in 1918–1931 to the designs of the architecture firm Delano & Aldrich.

way/266940107.name: The Jewish Museum
way/266940107.intro: The Jewish Museum is an art museum housed at 1109 Fifth Avenue, in the Felix M. Warburg House. It holds a collection of approximately 30,000 objects, including religious artifacts, fine art, and media.

way/266940614.name: Lucy Drexel Dahlgren House
way/266940614.intro: The Lucy Drexel Dahlgren House is a historic home located at 15 East 96th Street between Fifth and Madison Avenues in Manhattan, New York City. It was built in 1915–16 for Lucy Wharton Drexel Dahlgren.

way/269290359.name: Central Savings Bank Building
way/269290359.intro: The Apple Bank Building, also known as the Central Savings Bank Building and 2100 Broadway, is a bank and residential building at 2100–2114 Broadway. Constructed as a branch of the Central Savings Bank, now Apple Bank, from 1926 to 1928, it was designed by York and Sawyer.

way/270975149.name: Soldiers' and Sailors' Monument
way/270975149.intro: The Soldiers' and Sailors' Memorial Monument is located in Riverside Park, at the intersection of 89th Street and Riverside Drive. It commemorates Union Army soldiers and sailors who served in the American Civil War and was completed May 26, 1902.

way/271205008.name: Nicholas Roerich Museum
way/271205008.intro: The Nicholas Roerich Museum is a museum on the Upper West Side of Manhattan in New York City, dedicated to the works of Nicholas Roerich (1874–1947), a Russian-born cosmopolitan artist.

way/271220752.name: Museum of the City of New York
way/271220752.intro: The Museum of the City of New York (MCNY) is a history and art museum in Manhattan, New York City. It was founded by Henry Collins Brown in 1923 to preserve and present the history of New York City and its people.
way/271220752.source_title: Museum of the City of New York

way/271274003.name: El Museo Del Barrio
way/271274003.intro: El Museo del Barrio at 1230 Fifth Avenue in Upper Manhattan, New York City was founded in 1969. It specializes in Latin American and Caribbean art, with an emphasis on works from Puerto Rico and the Puerto Rican community in New York City.

way/271625750.name: Langston Hughes House
way/271625750.intro: The Langston Hughes House is a historic home located in Harlem, Manhattan, New York City. Noted African American poet and author Langston Hughes (1902–1967) occupied the top floor as his workroom from 1947 to 1967.

way/271827575.name: Abyssinian Baptist Church
way/271827575.intro: The Abyssinian Baptist Church is a Baptist megachurch located at 132 West 138th Street in the Harlem neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City. It is affiliated with the National Baptist Convention, USA and American Baptist Churches USA.

way/271885447.name: Hamilton Grange National Memorial
way/271885447.intro: Hamilton Grange National Memorial is a historic house museum within St. Nicholas Park in the Hamilton Heights neighborhood of Manhattan in New York City, United States. It was the only home ever owned by Alexander Hamilton, a U.S. founding father.

way/271922197.name: General Grant National Memorial
way/271922197.intro: Grant's Tomb, officially the General Grant National Memorial, is the final resting place of Ulysses S. Grant and of his wife Julia. The structure is in the median of Riverside Drive at 122nd Street, just east of Riverside Park.

way/275014150.name: Morris-Jumel Mansion
way/275014150.intro: The Morris–Jumel Mansion is an 18th-century historic house museum in the Washington Heights neighborhood of Upper Manhattan in New York City, United States. It is the oldest extant house in Manhattan, built in 1765 by British military officer Roger Morris.

way/277904719.name: New York County Lawyers Association
way/277904719.intro: The New York County Lawyers' Association Building is at 14 Vesey Street between Broadway and Church Street. It was built in 1929–30 and was designed by architect Cass Gilbert in the English Georgian style.
way/277904719.source_title: New York County Lawyers' Association Building

way/277904752.name: Saint Paul's Chapel
way/277904752.intro: St. Paul's Chapel is a chapel building of Trinity Church, an Episcopal parish, at 209 Broadway, between Fulton Street and Vesey Street, in Lower Manhattan, New York City. Built in 1766, it is the oldest surviving church building in Manhattan.

way/278053530.name: New York Stock Exchange
way/278053530.intro: The New York Stock Exchange Building is the headquarters of the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE), located in the Financial District of Lower Manhattan in New York City.

way/278076368.name: 100 Old Slip - New York City Police Museum
way/278076368.intro: The New York City Police Museum (NYCPM) is a museum about the history and contributions of the New York City Police Department. Founded in 1999, the museum is located in Lower Manhattan in New York City, with one of the museum's primary focuses a memorial to the September 11 attacks.

way/278346578.name: MoMA
way/278346578.intro: The Museum of Modern Art (MoMA) is an art museum located in Midtown Manhattan, New York City, on 53rd Street between Fifth and Sixth Avenues. MoMA's collection spans the late 19th century to the present, and includes over 200,000 works.

way/278353405.name: Circle Line
way/278353405.intro: Circle Line Sightseeing Cruises is a boat-based sightseeing and entertainment company in Manhattan, New York. It operates guided tours of New York City from its base at Pier 83 in the Hell's Kitchen neighborhood.

way/278396518.name: Liggett Hall
way/278396518.intro: Liggett Hall, also known as Building 400, is a former barracks building designed by McKim, Mead & White and built in 1929 near Fort Jay on Governors Island in New York Harbor, in New York City. It measures 1,023 feet (312 m) long.

way/280850916.name: Weehawken Water Tower
way/280850916.intro: This brick water tower is part of the Hackensack Water Company Complex in Weehawken, New Jersey, registered in the U.S. National Register of Historic Places. The Hackensack Water Company moved its headquarters to Weehawken in Hudson County and set up offices in the tower.

way/284880674.name: Blackwell House
way/284880674.intro: Blackwell House is a historic house on Roosevelt Island in New York City. It was built by Jacob Blackwell in 1796 and added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1972.

way/286996622.name: University Woods Park
way/286996622.intro: University Woods, also known as Cedar Park, is a small woodland park in the University Heights neighborhood of the Bronx in New York City. A restoration project was begun in 2008 by the Friends of the Woods organization, with a $500,000 grant from Mayor Michael Bloomberg.

way/287462475.name: Bellevue South Park
way/287462475.intro: Bellevue South Park is a 1.59-acre (0.64 ha) public park in the Kips Bay neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City. It was originally planned as part of the Bellevue South Urban Renewal Area approved by New York City in 1964.

way/288749896.name: Whitney Museum of American Art
way/288749896.intro: The Whitney Museum of American Art is a modern and contemporary American art museum in Manhattan in New York City. The institution was founded in 1930 by Gertrude Vanderbilt Whitney.

way/29185374.name: Smallpox Hospital
way/29185374.intro: The Smallpox Hospital was a hospital located on Roosevelt Island in Manhattan, New York City. Designed by architect James Renwick Jr., the 100-bed hospital opened in 1856, when the area was known as Blackwell's Island.

way/296038615.name: Harlem Fire Watchtower
way/296038615.intro: The Harlem Fire Watchtower, also known as the Mount Morris Fire Watchtower, is a fire lookout tower at Marcus Garvey Park in Harlem, Manhattan, New York City. It is the only survivor of 11 cast-iron watchtowers placed throughout the city starting in the 1850s.

way/296157576.name: Prison Ship Martyrs Monument
way/296157576.intro: The Prison Ship Martyrs' Monument is a war memorial at Fort Greene Park, in the New York City borough of Brooklyn. It commemorates more than 11,500 American prisoners of war who died in captivity aboard sixteen British prison ships during the American Revolutionary War.

way/308329352.name: Broadway
way/308329352.intro: Broadway is a street and major thoroughfare in the U.S. state of New York.

way/31009822.name: Stuyvesant Cove Park
way/31009822.intro: Stuyvesant Cove Park is a 1.9-acre (7,700 m2) public park that runs from 18th Street to 23rd Street between the FDR Drive and the East River. Part of the East River Greenway, it connects to the Captain Patrick J. Brown Walk on the south end.

way/318328998.name: Frederick Douglass Circle
way/318328998.intro: Frederick Douglass Circle is a traffic circle at the northwest corner of Central Park at Eighth Avenue and 110th Street. It is named for Frederick Douglass.

way/329988114.name: Verdi Square
way/329988114.intro: Verdi Square is a 0.1-acre (400 m2) park on a trapezoidal traffic island on the Upper West Side of Manhattan in New York City. Named for Italian opera composer Giuseppe Verdi, it is bounded by 72nd Street, 73rd Street, Broadway, and Amsterdam Avenue.

way/33819583.name: Marsha P. Johnson State Park
way/33819583.intro: Marsha P. Johnson State Park is an 11-acre (4.5 ha) state park in the Williamsburg neighborhood of Brooklyn in New York City, New York, U.S. The park stretches along the East River near North 7th, 8th, and 9th Streets, with views of the Williamsburg Bridge and Midtown Manhattan.

way/33819642.name: Monsignor McGolrick Park
way/33819642.intro: Monsignor McGolrick Park is located in Greenpoint, Brooklyn, in New York City. It is between Driggs Avenue to the south, Russell Street to the west, Nassau Avenue to the north, and Monitor Street to the east.

way/343765233.name: Peter Detmold Park
way/343765233.intro: Peter Detmold Park is a 0.59-acre (0.24 ha) public park in the Turtle Bay neighborhood of Manhattan, New York, United States. The park runs from East 49th to 51st streets and was named after Peter Detmold in 1972.

way/34633854.name: Empire State Building
way/34633854.intro: The Empire State Building is a 102-story, supertall skyscraper in the Midtown South neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City, United States. The building was designed in the Art Deco style by Shreve, Lamb & Harmon and constructed between 1930 and 1931.

way/352412115.name: MacDougal-Sullivan Gardens Historic District
way/352412115.intro: The MacDougal–Sullivan Gardens Historic District is a small historic district of twenty-two houses at 74–96 MacDougal Street and 170–188 Sullivan Street between Houston and Bleecker Streets.

way/362679830.name: Smiling Hogshead Ranch
way/362679830.intro: Smiling Hogshead Ranch (SHR) is a community garden located in Long Island City in New York City. Originally formed in 2011 by Gil Lopez, it was originally a guerilla garden on the abandoned tracks for the Degnon Terminal tracks, a spur off the Montauk Cutoff.

way/365936496.name: Ascenzi Square
way/365936496.intro: Ascenzi Square is a small plaza in the Williamsburg neighborhood of Brooklyn, New York City. On March 29, 1939, it was designated in honor of brothers Joseph and William Ascenzi, residents of Williamsburg who were killed in the First World War.

way/367660740.name: Roberto Clemente State Park
way/367660740.intro: Roberto Clemente State Park is a 25-acre (10 ha) state park in Morris Heights, Bronx, New York City. It is adjacent to the Harlem River, the Major Deegan Expressway, and the Morris Heights station on Metro-North's Hudson Line.

way/36865288.name: Desalvio Playground
way/36865288.intro: DeSalvio Playground is a neighborhood park located on the corner of Spring Street and Mulberry Street in NoLita, in Manhattan, New York City.

way/370574294.name: MoMA PS1
way/370574294.intro: MoMA PS1 is a contemporary art museum at 22-01 Jackson Avenue in the Long Island City neighborhood of Queens, in New York City, United States. It has been affiliated with the Museum of Modern Art since January 2000.

way/372721441.name: Teardrop Park
way/372721441.intro: Teardrop Park is a 1.8-acre (0.7 ha) public park in lower Manhattan, in Battery Park City, near the site of the World Trade Center. It was designed by Michael Van Valkenburgh Associates and includes art designed for it by Ann Hamilton.

way/375157262.name: Brooklyn Bridge
way/375157262.intro: The Brooklyn Bridge is a cable-stayed suspension bridge in New York City, spanning the East River between the boroughs of Manhattan and Brooklyn. Opened on May 24, 1883, it was the first fixed crossing of the East River.

way/378359193.name: Vincent F. Albano Jr. Playground
way/378359193.intro: Vincent F. Albano Jr. Playground is a 0.35-acre (0.14 ha) public park in the Kips Bay neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City. It is at the northwest corner of Second Avenue and East 29th Street and opened in 1967.

way/383689939.name: The Noguchi Museum
way/383689939.intro: The Noguchi Museum is at 32-37 Vernon Boulevard in the Long Island City neighborhood of Queens in New York City. Designed and created by Isamu Noguchi (1904–1988), it opened on a limited basis to the public in 1985.

way/385106972.name: Ralph Bunche Park
way/385106972.intro: Ralph Bunche Park is a small municipal public park in the Turtle Bay neighborhood of New York City. Originally referred to as United Nations Plaza Park, it was named in 1979 for Ralph Bunche.

way/387380393.name: Nutter's Battery
way/387380393.intro: Nutter's Battery is in the North Woods of Central Park in Manhattan, New York City, overlooking the Harlem Meer. The battery was built during the War of 1812 and was named after Valentine Nutter, who owned the surrounding property.

way/388436810.name: American Museum of Natural History
way/388436810.intro: The American Museum of Natural History (AMNH) is a natural history museum on the Upper West Side of Manhattan in New York City. The museum complex comprises 21 interconnected buildings housing 45 permanent exhibition halls, in addition to a planetarium and a library.

way/39243853.name: Morningside Park
way/39243853.intro: Morningside Park is a 30-acre (12-hectare) public park in Upper Manhattan in New York City, New York, United States. It is bounded by 110th Street to the south, 123rd Street to the north, Morningside Avenue to the east, and Morningside Drive to the west.

way/39243913.name: Blockhouse No. 1
way/39243913.intro: Blockhouse No. 1, colloquially known as The Blockhouse, is a small fort in the North Woods section of Central Park, Manhattan, New York City. Finished in 1814, it is the second-oldest structure in the park, after Cleopatra's Needle.

way/40336168.name: Claremont Park
way/40336168.intro: Claremont Park is a park in the Morrisania section of the Bronx in New York City. The land was once part of the Morris family estate and was the site of the Zborowski Mansion.

way/40336208.name: Saint Mary's Park
way/40336208.intro: St. Mary's Park is a public park in the Mott Haven neighborhood in the South Bronx section of The Bronx, New York City. The park has sporting facilities and an indoor recreation center.

way/40416347.name: Carroll Park
way/40416347.intro: Carroll Park is a nearly 117-acre (47 ha) public park located in the historic Washington Village-Pigtown neighborhood in southwestern Baltimore, Maryland.

way/40709911.name: Commodore Barry Park
way/40709911.intro: Commodore Barry Park is an urban park in the Fort Greene neighborhood of the New York City borough of Brooklyn. It was acquired in 1836 by the Village of Brooklyn and named for Commodore John Barry in 1951.

way/410310399.name: Coleman Playground
way/410310399.intro: Coleman Playground is a public park on the border between the Chinatown and Lower East Side neighborhoods of Manhattan in New York City.

way/413055246.name: City Hall Park
way/413055246.intro: City Hall Park is a public park surrounding New York City Hall in the Civic Center of Manhattan. It was the town commons of the nascent city of New York.

way/47798671.name: Queensbridge Park
way/47798671.intro: Queensbridge Park, named for the nearby Queensboro Bridge, is a 20.34-acre (8.23 ha) city park along the East River in Long Island City, Queens, New York City. The park has a riverfront promenade, baseball diamonds, running paths, lawns and areas for picnicking.

way/48869328.name: United Nations Headquarters

way/497484756.name: Albert Capsouto Park
way/497484756.intro: Albert Capsouto Park is a triangular-shaped pocket park in the Tribeca neighborhood of Lower Manhattan in New York City. It is bounded by Canal Street to the northeast, Varick Street to the west, and Laight Street to the south.

way/498671779.name: Drumgoole Plaza
way/498671779.intro: Drumgoole Plaza is a public park below the ramps to the Brooklyn Bridge on Frankfort Street between Park Row and Gold Street. Opened on November 5, 2003, it is maintained by Pace under the management of the New York City Department of Parks and Recreation.

way/5029111.name: Battery Park
way/5029111.intro: The Battery, formerly known as Battery Park, is a 25-acre (10 ha) public park at the southern tip of Manhattan Island. The park contains Castle Clinton, multiple monuments and the SeaGlass Carousel.

way/50603780.name: USS Intrepid
way/50603780.intro: USS Intrepid (CV/CVA/CVS-11), also known as The Fighting "I", is one of 24 Essex-class aircraft carriers built during World War II for the United States Navy. She is the fourth US Navy ship to bear the name.

way/516204836.intro: Bridge Park is a park in the Bronx, New York. Its name references its proximity to Alexander Hamilton Bridge, Washington Bridge, and High Bridge.

way/517205427.name: Astoria Park
way/517205427.intro: Astoria Park is a 59.96-acre (24.26 ha) public park in the Astoria neighborhood of Queens in New York City. It contains a playground, a soccer field, a running track, a skate park, and courts for tennis, basketball, and bocce.

way/53142768.name: USS Growler
way/53142768.intro: USS Growler (SSG-577) was built to deliver the Regulus I cruise missile. It is the second and final submarine of the Grayback class.

way/531580782.intro: Robert Moses Playground is a 1.3-acre (0.53 ha) playground and park in Manhattan, New York City. It is located in the Murray Hill neighborhood on First Avenue between 41st and 42nd streets, immediately south of the headquarters of the United Nations.

way/538080002.name: Elizabeth H. Berger Plaza
way/538080002.intro: Elizabeth H. Berger Plaza is a public park in the Financial District of Manhattan, New York City. Formerly known as the Edgar Street Greenstreet, it honors Elizabeth H. Berger (1960–2013) and is located on the site of Little Syria.

way/544675664.name: Mitchel Square
way/544675664.intro: Mitchel Square Park is a small urban park in the Washington Heights neighborhood of the New York City borough of Manhattan. It is named in honor of former mayor John Purroy Mitchel and formed by the intersection of Saint Nicholas Avenue, Broadway and 167th Street.

way/565419878.name: Lorelei Fountain
way/565419878.intro: The Lorelei Fountain, also known as the Heinrich Heine Memorial, is on East 161st Street in the Concourse section of the Bronx, New York City. It was unveiled in 1899 and is dedicated to German poet and writer Heinrich Heine.

way/580123906.name: Mulry Square
way/580123906.intro: Mulry Square is a triangular site at the southwest corner of Greenwich Avenue and Seventh Avenue South. It was once thought to be the site of a wedge-shaped diner that was the inspiration for Edward Hopper's painting Nighthawks.

way/585788256.name: Central Park Carousel
way/585788256.intro: The Central Park Carousel, officially the Michael Friedsam Memorial Carousel, is a vintage wood-carved carousel located in Central Park in Manhattan, New York City. It is the fourth carousel on the site where it is located.

way/586476446.name: Madame Tussauds New York
way/586476446.intro: Madame Tussauds New York is a tourist attraction located on 42nd Street in the Times Square neighborhood of Midtown Manhattan in New York City. The Madame Tussauds New York location opened on November 15, 2000, after seven years of planning.

way/608947452.name: Christopher Columbus Monument
way/608947452.intro: The Columbus Monument is a 76-foot (23 m) column in the center of Columbus Circle in New York City honoring the Italian explorer Christopher Columbus, who first made an expedition to the New World in 1492. The monument was created by Italian sculptor Gaetano Russo in 1892.

way/608955193.name: The Peace Fountain
way/608955193.intro: The Peace Fountain is a 40-foot-high (12 m) sculpture and fountain located next to the Cathedral of St. John the Divine in the Morningside Heights section of Manhattan in New York City. It was commissioned in 1985 by Greg Wyatt, sculptor-in-residence at the cathedral.

way/608965023.name: USS Maine Monument
way/608965023.intro: The USS Maine National Monument is located at the Merchants' Gate entrance to Central Park, at Columbus Circle, in Manhattan, New York City. It was dedicated on May 30, 1913 to the men killed aboard USS Maine (ACR-1) when the ship exploded in Havana Harbor.
